name: Tiroler Schnapsmuseum Pill
kurzbeschreibung: The Tiroler Schnapsmuseum in Pill near Schwaz: historic Plankenhof palace distillery with copper stills and tastings of fine fruit brandies.
beschreibung:
Overview

The traditional Tiroler Schnapsmuseum is located within the historic estate of the traditional inn Plankenhof in the picturesque Unterinntal village of Pill near Schwaz (Schwaz district) at an altitude of approximately 556 metres. Situated right at the foot of the Kellerjoch mountain and at the gateway to the Zillertal valley, this specialised museum immerses visitors in centuries of alpine distilling heritage. In the venerable vaulted cellars of this heritage-listed estate, the masterful art of distilling noble Tyrolean high-altitude fruits, wild berries, and roots into premium fruit brandies and liqueurs is vividly showcased.

Route & Requirements

Schnapps distilling in Tyrol looks back on a royal heritage officially granted by the imperial court: back in the 18th century, Empress Maria Theresia bestowed the historic "right to distill" (Brennrecht) upon many Tyrolean mountain farmers to preserve their bountiful fruit harvests and safeguard their survival during harsh mountain winters. At the Tiroler Schnapsmuseum, visitors wander through historical vaulted cellars and an authentically preserved historic palace distillery. On display are heavy copper distilling alembics spanning multiple centuries, ancient oak barrels, historical alcoholometers, manual bottling machines, and antique recipe ledgers. Expert distillers explain the sophisticated process from meticulous fruit mashing through heads, hearts, and tails during double distillation, all the way to years of barrel aging. Following the tour, guests enjoy a guided tasting of exquisite Tyrolean specialties in the rustic tasting parlour: alongside classics such as Tiroler Obstler, rowanberry (Vogelbeere), and Williamsbirne pear brandy, rare alpine specialties including masterwort (Meisterwurz), gentian spirit (Enzianbrand), and fine Swiss pine liqueur (Tiroler Zirbenlik?r) can be savoured.

Visit & Arrival

The Tiroler Schnapsmuseum at Plankenhof is open year-round from Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 18:00 (Sundays upon request; guided tours with tasting take place several times daily). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): guided tour including tasting of three fine spirits approx. ?6.50 for adults, alcohol-free participation approx. ?3.50, children accompanied by adults free. The adjoining farm shop is freely accessible. Getting there by car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Vomp or Schwaz), then continue along the Tiroler Bundesstra?e B171 directly to Pill; extensive free parking is available directly at Gasthof Plankenhof (Dorf 7). By public transport: take ?BB train to Schwaz or Pill-Vomperbach station, where regional VVT bus line 4111 runs every half hour directly to the Pill Gemeindeamt stop (only a two-minute walk away).

Tips

The historic vaulted cellars of the museum are reached via a few steps; the farm shop and the ground-floor tasting parlour are barrier-free and fully accessible. After the tasting, we highly recommend stopping for a meal at the traditional restaurant of Gasthof Plankenhof, renowned for its Zillertaler Krapfen and authentic Tyrolean delicacies. All sampled spirits and liqueurs can be purchased as exclusive souvenirs in the farm shop.
